title: Signed URLs, public access and the bucket that leaked

videos.script: Everything in Quitanda's buckets is private. This lesson is about keeping it that way, and about the few ways it stops being true. {{private}} First, the signed URL. It hands one person one file, with no account, until it expires. {{url}} You will sign one with a key made on your own laptop, for an account that does not exist, and see that the URL carries the permission itself. {{sign}} Then the switches that keep a bucket from ever becoming public: uniform access, public access prevention, and the organisation policies above them. {{switches}} The emulator accepts every one of them and keeps none. You will watch a request with no credentials read a private report. {{none}} And finally the bucket that leaked. The exposures that made the news were nearly always a line somebody wrote: a grant, an access list, or a link that lived too long. {{leak}} You will learn how each one happens, how to prevent it, how to find out, and the one check worth running from outside. {{check}}
